Messages.Body:
I've been trying to make a decent deck focused on the Harbingers ever
since Bloodlines came out, but I haven't been very successful so far.
I'll list my most recent deck here for you guys to tear apart and
hopefully we can get to something that actually works. Any links to
good Harbingers decks would also be helpful. Thanks! :o)

The basic concept may be too unfocused... or maybe it's just lame.
The idea was to get some fortitude weenies that could block for a
while until they can equip with a Faithful Servant (no one seems to
block that) and then bleed/Force of Will. If they get a blood doll, I
have a weak bloat working as long as I can intercept and protect them.
And I might be able to rescue them later if I need them for some
reason (swarm bleed?).

The other thought was to use Summon Soul to keep bringing out Sudden
Reversal, Renewed Vigor and other good cards.

Other than that, I can't remeber where this deck was heading or why
it's so lame (not much pressure on my prey, no real votes, weak bleed,
etc.). I seem to have taken a lot of the good cards out to put in
other decks, so maybe something crucial is missing from the original.

If you have any thoughts, suggestions, or even humorous flames, that
would be great.

Cheers,
Howard

On 21 Jun 2002 18:32:44 -0700, hdma...@hotmail.com (HD) wrote:
>I put together a similar version of the deck you listed above. I'm
>missing a few of the cards, but it's pretty close to what you had in
>that deck. Now I'm wondering how you play it (basic strategy) and if
>there are any important tips you would suggest.

Take it slow. Your prey will be dragging with the effects of the
Meddling of Semsith. None of your Cardinal Benedictions can afford to
fail, so double and triple check the voting situation before you
attempt to call them. Only use Agaitas' ability if you have the
Barrens (or the Fragment) in play. If you can't immediately use the
drawn card, discard it, and you will get the card you would have drawn
from your deck right away. Pool gain is critical, so the
Consanguineous Boons and Ancient Influence need to pass. Political
Strangehold is nice if you get it at the end of the game, but it is a
good idea to call it and make it fail at the beginning if anyone else
at the table is playing with large vampires. Try to get the Erebus
Mask and the Legendary Vampire on the same minion, a three bleed at
one built in stealth is nothing to sneeze at. Be careful with it
though, if your grand-prey can't block, have that vampire calling your
votes at two stealth.

The Sanguine Instructions should give Agaitas superior fortitude, or
give superior Auspex to Gisela or Anisa. Agaitas cannot be a Cardinal
without the Sanguine Instruction though, so don't give it to the girls
until he is at seven capacity where he needs to be.

Intercept as little as you can. If your vampires cannot act, you
cannot win. If you will be ousted though, you have two intercept or
can use the bleed bounce as an additional offense.

Carpe noctem.

Lasombra

http://www.TheLasombra.com
